name: claude-bridge
description: Mirror and control Claude Code sessions from your phone — direct, no servers. LAN + p2p tunnel (iroh).
readme_summary: Claude Bridge allows users to mirror and control their Claude Code terminal sessions directly from an Android phone. It establishes a direct connection between the phone and the PC, either over a local network or via a p2p tunnel, eliminating the need for servers.
key_features: Support for multiple sessions and paired PCs
Push notifications for Claude Code hooks
Persistent sessions that survive bridge restarts
primary_use_case: Remote control and monitoring of Claude Code sessions from a mobile device without relying on cloud infrastructure.
cover_image_prompt: A split scene: on one side, a person's hand holding a smartphone displaying a vibrant, interactive terminal interface. On the other side, a desktop computer screen also showing the identical terminal session, with subtle digital tendrils connecting the phone and PC. The phone's screen should have a glowing aura, symbolizing direct control, while the PC side shows a 'keeper' process icon ensuring session persistence. The background is a clean, modern workspace, with a subtle 'Claude Bridge' logo integrated into the scene. The overall style should be a clean, 3D isometric illustration with a focus on the seamless connection and mirroring of the terminal.

name: MeshSense
description: MeshSense directly connects to your Meshtastic node via Bluetooth or WiFi and continuously provides information to assess the health of your mesh network.
readme_summary: MeshSense is an open-source application written in TypeScript that monitors, maps, and graphically displays the vital statistics of Meshtastic mesh networks. It connects via Bluetooth or WiFi to provide insights into network health, including connected nodes, signal reports, and trace routes.
key_features: Maps and graphically displays network stats
Provides node information, signal reports, and trace routes
Supports headless usage via command-line flags and environment variables
Provides development setup instructions for UI and API services
primary_use_case: Monitoring and visualizing the health and status of Meshtastic mesh networks.
cover_image_prompt: A friendly, stylized robot with a magnifying glass and a network cable, examining a glowing, interconnected web of nodes. The robot is pointing its magnifying glass at a specific node, which displays a small, clear health status icon (like a green checkmark or a yellow warning). Data streams, represented by glowing lines and small digital particles, flow between the nodes, illustrating network activity. In the background, a subtle, simplified map shows the geographical spread of the nodes. The overall mood is informative and reassuring, with a clean, modern aesthetic. The style should be a 3D isometric illustration with bright, clear colors and soft lighting, emphasizing clarity and accessibility.

name: PdfDing
description: Selfhosted PDF manager, viewer and editor offering a seamless user experience on multiple devices.
readme_summary: PdfDing is a self-hosted PDF management, viewing, and editing solution designed for seamless cross-device access. It offers features like workspaces, tagging, highlighting, and SSO, all accessible through a clean, intuitive web interface.
key_features: Browser-based PDF viewing with position memory
Workspaces, collections, multi-level tagging, starring, and archiving
Clean UI with dark mode and customization
primary_use_case: Self-hosted management, viewing, and editing of PDF documents across multiple devices.
cover_image_prompt: A librarian meticulously organizing a vast, multi-tiered library filled with glowing PDF books. Each book has a small bookmark indicating its reading progress. The librarian is using a magical tablet to add colorful highlights and annotations to an open book, while other books are neatly sorted into distinct 'workspaces' represented by floating shelves. Subtle digital particles flow from the tablet, symbolizing data management. The repository name 'PdfDing' is subtly etched on the library's main archway. The scene is rendered in a warm, inviting 3D isometric illustration style with clear iconography and a focus on organization and accessibility.

name: RS-Key
description: Open-source FIDO2, OpenPGP, PIV and OATH security-key firmware for RP2350, written in Rust
readme_summary: RS-Key is an open-source, Rust-based firmware for the Raspberry Pi RP2350, transforming it into a versatile security key. It supports FIDO2, OpenPGP, PIV, and OATH protocols, enabling secure authentication and cryptographic operations. The project is experimental and intended for development and research, emphasizing its limitations and the need for careful threat modeling.
key_features: FIDO2 / WebAuthn / U2F support (passkeys, 2FA, ssh ed25519-sk)
OpenPGP card 3.4 support (gpg signing, decryption, authentication)
Trusted display variant for on-device PIN and approval prompts
primary_use_case: To provide open-source, customizable firmware for the Raspberry Pi RP2350 to function as a multi-protocol security key for authentication and cryptographic operations, primarily for development, research, and controlled experiments.
cover_image_prompt: A stylized, glowing Raspberry Pi RP2350 chip at the center, acting as a digital 'master key'. From the chip, streams of light flow outwards, transforming into various security icons: a padlock for FIDO2, a quill for OpenPGP, a shield for PIV, and a clock for OATH. These streams are being securely channeled into a digital vault. Subtle UI elements showing cryptographic symbols and data streams are visible around the chip. The background is a clean, abstract digital landscape with a soft blue and green color palette. The overall style is a 3D isometric illustration with a futuristic, secure feel, emphasizing the transformation of raw hardware into a versatile security tool. The repository name 'RS-Key' is subtly integrated into the vault's design.

name: DracoLure
description: DracoLure — Dragon Vector Honeypot: polyglot deception honeypot with real-time detection, threat scoring, and quarantine.
readme_summary: DracoLure is a polyglot deception honeypot designed to lure, detect, score, and quarantine malicious attackers in real-time. It serves believable bait to keep attackers engaged while analyzing their probes against a signature library, assigning threat scores, and automatically blocking hostile sources.
key_features: Automated quarantine and blocking of hostile sources
Serves believable bait (fake corporate portal, /.env, wp-login, etc.)
primary_use_case: To act as a deceptive security honeypot that lures and analyzes malicious network traffic, identifying and blocking threats in real-time.
cover_image_prompt: A vigilant dragon guarding a treasure hoard filled with glowing digital data streams. The dragon's eyes glow with a scanning light, analyzing incoming shadowy figures attempting to breach the hoard. When a shadowy figure is identified as a threat, the dragon breathes a stream of fire, creating a shimmering, impenetrable barrier that quarantines the figure. Small, stylized icons representing various attack vectors (like SQL injection, XSS) are subtly embedded in the background. The scene is set in a dark, mystical cave illuminated by the glow of the data and the dragon's fire. The overall style is a 3D isometric illustration with a dark fantasy aesthetic, emphasizing the protective and deceptive nature of the honeypot. The repository name 'DracoLure' is subtly etched on a nearby rock.

name: RadioGuessr
description: A GeoGuessr-style game where you tune into live radio streams from around the world and test your geography skills by guessing their broadcasting location on an interactive 3D globe.
readme_summary: RadioGuessr is a web-based game inspired by GeoGuessr, where players listen to live radio streams from around the world and guess their origin location on an interactive 3D globe. It utilizes the Radio Browser API for streams and globe.gl for visualization, offering features like hints, rerolls, and session history.
key_features: Global Radio Exploration via Radio Browser API
Multiple Visual Themes for the globe
Enhanced Mobile UI with Tailwind CSS and Framer Motion
Talk Mode for prioritizing talk radio
primary_use_case: A fun and educational web game for users to test their geography knowledge and explore global radio stations.
cover_image_prompt: A stylized, vintage radio receiver sits on a desk, emitting sound waves that transform into glowing lines connecting to various points on a vibrant, interactive 3D globe. The globe displays subtle country borders and highlighted locations. Small, translucent UI elements showing a score and a 'guess' button float near the radio. The background is a soft, abstract representation of a world map. The overall mood is playful and exploratory, with a clean, modern illustration style. The repository name 'RadioGuessr' is subtly integrated into the design of the radio's dial.
